thm:spectral-compressions.title: Strong and norm-multiplicative spectral compressions
thm:spectral-compressions.note: Proved for the NCG.SpectralTriple encoding of compact-resolvent triples (A_D = smoothAlgebra) on a separable Hilbert space. (1) spectral_compressions_strong: a sequence P_n = diracSpectralScreen S (s n) of finite-rank orthogonal spectral projections of D (onto finitely many eigenspaces, via the compact normal resolvent), increasing (P_{n+1}P_n = P_n, ranges increase), preserving dom D and commuting with D, with P_n -> I strongly, P_n T P_n -> T strongly for EVERY bounded T (in particular pi(a), the bounded extension of [D,pi(a)] and the resolvents) and product defects P_nTP_nUP_n - P_nTUP_n -> 0 strongly (eq:strong-compression-topology); the sequence is extracted from the Finset-indexed screen net using a dense sequence (exists_monotone_screens). (2) compressed_commutator_identity (eq:compressed-commutator-identity): for x in P H, P D (P pi(a) x) - P pi(a) P D x = P (D pi(a) x - pi(a) D x) (and = P C x for the bounded extension C, compressed_commutator_identity_of_extension). (3) normMultiplicative_iff_commutator_tendsto: along any screen sequence, ||P_n pi(ab) P_n - P_n pi(a) P_n pi(b) P_n|| -> 0 for all a,b in A_D iff ||[P_n, pi(a)]|| -> 0 for all a in A_D (general C*-algebra lemma normMultiplicativeOn_iff_commutatorDecayOn on star-closed subsets, commutator <-> corners). (4) hasNormMultiplicativeCompression_iff_spectrallyQuasidiagonal. (5) Properness: toeplitzTriple is an NCG.SpectralTriple on the separable l^2(N) (number operator: symmetric, normal compact resolvent; A_D = StarAlgebra.adjoin {S}, all of whose elements have bounded commutators since [N,S] = S, [N,S*] = -S* and the bounded-commutator operators form a star subalgebra) which is not spectrally quasidiagonal (every nonzero finite spectral screen has ||[P,S]|| >= 1), packaged in spectrallyQuasidiagonal_proper; it is in the strong class by (1). Scope/rendering: NCG.SpectralTriple carries no real structure J or grading gamma, so 'equivariantly for J and gamma when marked' / 'symmetric cutoffs preserve the J, gamma signs' are not encoded; spectral projections are finite unions of eigenspaces of D (the symmetric cutoffs 1_[-R,R](D) are special cases); P_n up-arrow I is rendered as P_{n+1}P_n = P_n plus strong convergence.

thm:essential-image.note: All three lines proved with the categories and functors of ReconstructionCategories.lean (def:reconstruction-categories), now that thm:spectral-compressions is proved. essential_image bundles: (1) EssIm(S_fin^cal) = Spec_fin (finiteReconstruction_essImage; recovery from commutator data plus q_S coordinates: finite_calibrated_recovery/_sharp). (3) X in EssIm(S_cpt^norm,cal) iff some spectral projection sequence has ||[P_n,pi(a)]|| -> 0 on A_D (normReconstruction_essImage_iff; transport of P_n along unitary equivalences proved), iff SpectralCompressionsSequential.SpectrallyQuasidiagonal X (spectralCommutatorDecay_iff_spectrallyQuasidiagonal: every finite-rank spectral projection 1_B(D) is a finite resolvent screen, via linear independence of eigenvectors). (4) strictness: the Toeplitz triple (A = alg(I,S,S*), number operator, as a CompactMarkedObject for every mark type; also a non-vacuity witness) is in the strong but not the norm essential image and is not sqd in either form. Recorded commutant coordinates of the constructed (C2) sources are the zero functionals (the source structure allows any). Scope/rendering (flag for author): in def:reconstruction-categories the (C2)/(C3) sources use arbitrary increasing finite-rank spectral projections 1_{B_n}(D), while eq:sqd asks for 'symmetric' projections, equivariant for J and gamma; ReconstructionCategories.IsSpectrallyQuasidiagonal encodes this as windows 1_{[-R,R]}(D). Line 3 is proved with sqd in the screen form under which thm:spectral-compressions was closed (SpectralCompressionsSequential.SpectrallyQuasidiagonal: finite spectral screens P_n increasing to I with ||[P_n,pi(a)]|| -> 0 on A_D, no J/gamma clause - NCG.SpectralTriple carries no J/gamma); the windowed equivariant form is proved to be contained in the norm essential image (sqdProperty_le_essImage_norm), but the reverse inclusion is false in general for the (C3) category as written: e.g. D with simple eigenvalues k and k+3/2 (k in N), A_D = C[T], T the involution swapping the k and k+3/2 eigenvectors, has [D,T] bounded, exact multiplicativity along the block-closed screens {0..n} u {3/2..n+3/2}, yet every window [-R,R] cuts the block floor(R), so ||[P,T]|| = 1 (informal, not formalized). So the literal paper equality EssIm(norm) = Spec^sqd holds only if 'symmetric' means self-adjoint (the reading of the proved parent) or if (C2)/(C3) are restricted to symmetric windows; the J/gamma-equivariance clause of eq:sqd is not carried by the (C3) sources. [Coordinator 2 Oct 2026] Accepted as proved under the reading 'symmetric spectral projections' = self-adjoint spectral projections 1_B(D) (the reading under which thm:spectral-compressions was proved). Manuscript query: if 'symmetric' means windows 1_{[-R,R]}(D), the norm line fails (informal counterexample: eigenvalues k, k+3/2 with T swapping pairs; block screens are multiplicative but every window cuts a block, ||[P,T]|| = 1); only the inclusion window-sqd ⊆ norm essential image is proved (sqdProperty_le_essImage_norm). The J/γ-equivariance clause of eq:sqd is vacuous for the encoded triples, which carry no J/γ marks.

def:supp-renewal-graph.title: Stationary finite Markov graph
def:supp-renewal-graph.note: Bundled structure StationaryRenewalGraph V: masses m_x > 0 with sum 1, rates k_xy >= 0 for x != y (diagonal normalized to 0, since the generator sum over y != x ignores it), the mass-stationarity equation sum_y (q_xy - q_yx) = 0 for q = m k, and connectedness (ConductanceConnected) of the positive support of c = (q+q^T)/2. Derived generator L f (x) = sum_{y != x} k_xy (f y - f x) (generator_eq_sum_erase), flux q, conductance c = symmetrizedConductance q, current j = (q - q^T)/2 with c symmetric, j antisymmetric, q = c + j and sum_y j_xy = 0. StationaryRenewalGraph.spectralization discharges the hypotheses of canonical_graph_spectralization (thm:supp-graph-square), so the Hodge-Dirac carriers dirac/differential/representation of the earlier encoding attach to every such graph. Scoped: real scalars, both orientations retained via V x V.

thm:supp-graph-square.title: Graph Hodge square and exact Lipschitz seminorm
thm:supp-graph-square.note: From positive masses, nonnegative stationary rates and connected conductance support: d^*d f = -(L f + L^dagger f) = -2 L_s f in vertex coordinates, ||[D,f]||^2 = max_x (1/m_x) sum_y c_xy |f(y)-f(x)|^2 for real f (stationary_rate_commutator_energy, stated as the sup norm of x -> (1/m_x) sum_y c_xy |f y - f x|^2), the kernel is exactly the constants, and the resulting Connes distance on V is a metric. The added carre-du-champ normalization L(f)^2 = 2||Gamma_s(f)||_inf with Gamma_s(f)(x) = (1/(2m_x)) sum_y c_xy |f(y)-f(x)|^2 (eq:supp-carre-du-champ) is the same sup norm rescaled by the positive constant 1/2 (norm_smul); it is not restated as a separate Lean lemma. Scoped: real-valued vertex functions.

cth:supp-extensive-kernel.note: Proved. Kernel formula dim ker D = 2e+2-n (natural-number spelling of 2e-n+2) for the block Dirac (v,w) -> (d^dagger w, d v) with dim V = n, dim W = 2e (both orientations retained), connectedness rendered as dim ker d = 1 (connected_graph_kernel_dimension); periodic A3 count 11n+2 for e = 6n (periodic_A3_kernel_dimension). Consequence (new): the limit operator is an arbitrary, possibly unbounded, partially defined operator T : H ->l.[K] H (LinearPMap) on a Hilbert space over K = R or C (RCLike); its kernel is partialKer T; compact resolvent = some bounded two-sided inverse R of T - z (IsResolventAt: range in the domain, right and left inverse) is a compact operator (HasCompactResolvent). 'Compatible cofinal limit retaining all zero modes' = a cofinal family of connected periodic A3 stages (dim V_k = n_k, dim W_k = 12 n_k, dim ker d_k = 1, n_k unbounded) with real-linear injections ker D_k -> ker T. retained_universal_oneform_zero_modes_no_compact_resolvent proves dim ker D_k = 11 n_k + 2, ker T not finite-dimensional, and no compact resolvent. Key step: ker T lies in the eigenspace of R(z) at the nonzero eigenvalue (-z)^{-1} (and is trivial if z = 0), which is finite-dimensional for compact R (Mathlib ContinuousLinearMap.finite_dimensional_eigenspace). Compatibility maps between stages and self-adjointness are not needed and not assumed (the Lean result is stronger). The old arithmetic stand-in periodic_A3_nullity_unbounded is no longer cited. Vacuity: hypotheses jointly satisfiable (e.g. T = 0 on an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space with any injections of the finite stage kernels); no Lean witness added. Standard axioms only.

lem:supp-A3-frame.title: $A_3$ tight-frame identity
lem:supp-A3-frame.note: sum_alpha alpha alpha^T = 8 I and (1/8) sum_alpha <v,alpha>^2 = |v|^2 are proved for the explicit twelve roots (+-e_i +- e_j) of A3 written in R^3 coordinates of W_0 rather than in the R^4 hyperplane presentation.

prop:A3-covariance.title: Jump covariance and the independent metric
prop:A3-covariance.note: Proved, with the scoping of thm:supp-A3-distance. The frame identity sum_alpha alpha alpha^T = 8 I for the twelve A3 roots in R^3 coordinates of W_0 is relational_flat_vacuum (energy form tight_frame_energy); with k_{alpha,h} = 1/(8h^2) the covariance Q_h = sum_alpha k_{alpha,h} (h alpha)(h alpha)^T = (1/8) sum_alpha alpha alpha^T = I is this identity times the scalar h^2/(8h^2) = 1/8 (arithmetic, not a separate lemma), hence independent of h. The distance d_g is flatDistance = infDist(x - y, Lambda) (flatDistance_eq_infDist), independent of lifts (distance_periodic_right, distance_comm); the infimum is attained (min) because the lattice is closed in a proper space (lattice_isClosed with Mathlib's IsClosed.exists_infDist_eq_dist; not stated as a separate lemma). Scoped: as in thm:supp-A3-distance, d_g is taken as the flat quotient metric directly; its identification with the Riemannian geodesic distance of g = Q_h^{-1} is not formalised (no Riemannian structure in Lean).

thm:supp-A3-finite.title: $A_3$ Hodge identities and smooth-function consistency
thm:supp-A3-finite.note: Proved. All four clauses on the actual finite periodic A3 graph (vertices V_h = h Lambda/Lambda as Fin 3 -> ZMod d, mesh h = 1/d, rates 1/(8h^2), masses h^3, root steps reduced modulo the period): (i) eq:supp-A3-Lip, L_h(f)^2 = max_x (1/(8h^2)) sum_alpha |f(x+h alpha)-f(x)|^2 (graphLipschitz_sample_sq_eq, previous pass); (ii) eq:supp-A3-square via the general stationary theorem (previous pass); (iii) NEW eq:supp-A3-Lip-convergence with the explicit constant C_{A3} = 4 + sum_i |b_i| = 4 + 3 sqrt 2: graphLipschitz_rate shows |L_h(F|V_h) - sup_M |grad F|| <= (4 + sum_i |b_i|) M_2 h for every lattice-periodic C^1 field F whose gradient is M_2-Lipschitz (sup_M |grad F| rendered as sSup of the range of |grad F|; since grad F is periodic this is the L^infinity norm on the torus). Ingredients: first-order Taylor remainder along each root via the mean-value inequality (rootDifference_error_le, |(F(x+h alpha)-F(x))/h - alpha.grad F| <= |alpha|^2 M_2 h = 2 M_2 h), the existing reverse-triangle/tight-frame estimate (sqrt_energy_error_le) giving a pointwise error 4 M_2 h, a mesh-covering lemma (exists_vertex_near: every point of the torus is within h sum_i |b_i| of a vertex after a lattice translation, via floors in the period basis and ZMod.val_intCast) and periodicity of the gradient (gradient_periodic) to compare the max over the mesh with the sup over the torus; (iv) NEW generator clause: tendstoUniformly_generator proves (L_h F)(x) := (1/(8h^2)) sum_alpha (F(x+h alpha)-F(x)) -> (1/2) Delta F uniformly on the torus as h -> 0+ for every lattice-periodic C^2 field (F, DF, D^2F with D^2F continuous; the Hessian is uniformly continuous by periodicity), with Delta F = sum_i D^2F(e_i,e_i); ingredients: uniform second-order Taylor remainder by two one-dimensional mean-value inequalities (second_order_remainder), cancellation of the linear terms (sum of the twelve roots is zero) and the polarized tight-frame identity sum_alpha B(alpha,alpha) = 8 sum_i B(e_i,e_i) for every bilinear form (sum_root_bilinear, lem:supp-A3-frame), giving (h^2/2) 8 Delta F /(8 h^2) = Delta F/2; generator_sample_eq identifies the sampled generator at the vertices with the finite-graph generator of eq:supp-A3-square applied to F|V_h. Renderings disclosed: the paper's C^2 norm enters the rate only through the Lipschitz constant of grad F, so the rate theorem takes that constant M_2 (<= |F|_{C^2}) as hypothesis; the generator limit is proved under C^2 (weaker than the paper's C^4) as uniform convergence without a rate, exactly as the theorem states (the O(h^2 |F|_{C^4}) rate mentioned only in the proof is not formalised).

lem:A3-periodic-triangulation.title: A periodic shape-regular $A_3$ triangulation
lem:A3-periodic-triangulation.note: Proved, in the library's Euclidean realization Space = R^3 of W_0 (period basis b_i = three roots, coordinates = T^{-1}, h = 1/d). New infrastructure KuhnLovaszExtensionExact: the Freudenthal-Kuhn (Lovasz) extension kuhnExt g u = int_0^1 g(floor(u + s 1)) ds of lattice data, proved to be the continuous piecewise-affine (P1) interpolant on the Kuhn simplices k + K_sigma, K_sigma = conv{0, e_s1, e_s1+e_s2, 1} (kuhnExt_eq_barycentric; mem_kuhnSimplex_iff identifies k + K_sigma with 1 >= t_s1 >= t_s2 >= t_s3 >= 0), with unit-step Lipschitz and floor-comparison estimates. Mesh (A3KuhnInterpolationExact, meshSimplex d k sigma = hT(k + K_sigma)): covering (exists_mem_meshSimplex), face-to-face intersection = convex hull of common vertices (mem_convexHull_common_meshVertices), invariance under the period lattice k -> k + d z (add_mem_meshSimplex_iff), shape regularity with h-independent constants (contains the ball of radius h/8 about the barycentre, diameter <= 6h), descent to M: vertices project onto V_h and every point of V_h is a vertex (meshVertex_sub_point_vertex_mem_lattice, point_eq_meshVertex), vertices of one simplex distinct in V_h and projection injective on each simplex for d >= 2, and for d >= 3 a simplex meets another in at most one lattice translate (lattice_translate_unique), so projected simplices intersect in single common faces; every mesh edge joins vertices differing by at most three root steps h*alpha (meshVertex_sub_eq_sum_root_steps, card_root_steps_le_three). Interpolant I_h f = interp d f: agrees with f on V_h, continuous, periodic, affine on every mesh simplex, |I_h f(q) - I_h f(p)| <= sqrt 24 L_h(f) |q - p| and ||D I_h f|| <= sqrt 24 L_h(f) everywhere (eq:A3-interpolation-bound; L_h(f) = graphLipschitz (mass d) (conductance d) f, via the single-root bound sqrt 8 h L_h and sum_i (T^{-1}w)_i^2 <= |w|^2). Cells Q_{h,x} = x + hT[0,1)^3 (cell d x): cell_eq (= point d x + h * fundamental cell), volume_cell (volume = h^3 times the volume of the fundamental cell T[0,1)^3, i.e. normalized Haar measure h^3), diameter <= 6h, partition of the torus (exists_add_mem_cell_index, index_eq_of_mem_cell, index_periodic). eq:A3-cell-interpolation-bound with C = 3 sqrt 8: |f-hat_h - I_h f| <= 3 sqrt 8 h L_h(f) everywhere, f-hat_h = A3PeriodicStepFunctionLift.lift (= f(x) on Q_{h,x}, lift_eq_of_mem_cell). Rendering notes: the triangulation property is stated as covering + face-to-face (intersection = conv of common vertices); the quotient simplicial structure is stated through lattice invariance, vertex projection, injectivity on simplices and uniqueness of the meeting translate (d >= 3) rather than through a separate simplicial-complex API on M. Standard axioms only.

lem:supp-A3-compactness.note: Proved (a3_interpolant_compactness). Mesh sizes h_n = 1/(m_n + 1) with m_n -> infinity (any admissible h_n = 1/d_n decreasing to 0, possibly along a subsequence of meshes); f_n : V_{h_n} -> R with L_{h_n}(f_n) = graphLipschitz <= 1 and f_n vanishing at some vertex (the paper's x_{0,n} -> x_0 is not needed, so the Lean hypothesis is weaker). Conclusion: a subsequence of the Kuhn piecewise-affine interpolants I_{h_n} f_n of lem:A3-periodic-triangulation (A3KuhnInterpolation.interp) converges uniformly on all of Space to a lattice-periodic F (a function on M) with |F z - F z'| <= d_g(z, z'); hence F is 1-Lipschitz (rendering of F in W^{1,infinity}(M): a periodic Lipschitz function), ||grad F|| <= 1 at every point, and F is differentiable with ||grad F|| <= 1 almost everywhere (eq:supp-A3-limit-Lip, via Rademacher). Proof: the interpolants are periodic and uniformly sqrt 24-Lipschitz (eq:A3-interpolation-bound) and anchored, so Arzela-Ascoli on the ball of radius 6 (containing a fundamental domain) plus periodicity gives uniform convergence on Space; the sharp constant comes from |f_n x - f_n y| <= d_n(x, y) (finite Connes distance) and the proved uniform Connes-to-flat convergence tendsto_distanceError_zero (thm:supp-A3-distance is proved in the ledger, cited as an unconditional theorem, not as a hypothesis), instead of the paper's weak-* / summation-by-parts argument. Non-vacuity example (zero functions on the full mesh sequence) included. Standard axioms only.

lem:A3-uniform-distance-smoothing.title: Uniform smoothing of the torus distance
lem:A3-uniform-distance-smoothing.note: Proved (a3_uniform_distance_smoothing). eps_0 = 1, C_M = 8 + int ||D eta_1||. For every centre y (a lift in the Euclidean realization Space of W_0) and 0 < eps < 1, F_{y,eps} = eta_eps * d_g(y, .) with eta_eps the normalized Mathlib bump of radii (eps/2, eps) is C^infinity, lattice periodic (descends to M), |F - d_g(y, .)| <= eps, ||DF|| <= 1, and |F(p)| + ||DF(p)|| + ||D^2 F(p)|| <= C_M eps^{-1} for every p (the C^2(M) norm rendered as the sup of |F| + ||DF|| + ||D^2F|| with D^2F = fderiv (fderiv F)). The eps^{-1} rate: new general lemma norm_fderiv_convolution_sub_le_of_lipschitz (D(k*f) is K int||Dk||-Lipschitz for compactly supported C^1 scalar k and K-Lipschitz f; one derivative on the kernel), and the exact scaling int||D eta_eps|| = eps^{-1} int||D eta_1|| (bumps with fixed radius ratio are rescalings, eta_eps(x) = eps^{-3} eta_1(x/eps), Haar change of variables). Rendering: d_g(y, .) instead of d_g(., y) (the distance is symmetric). Standard axioms only.

thm:supp-A3-distance.title: Connes-distance convergence on the periodic $A_3$ lattice
thm:supp-A3-distance.note: sup over vertex pairs of |d_h(x,y) - d_g(x,y)| -> 0 is proved with d_h the actual finite commutator-supremum Connes distance of the A3 graph triple and d_g = flatDistance = infDist(x - y, Lambda_A3) = min over lattice vectors of ||x - y + l|| (flatDistance_eq_infDist), exactly eq:A3-independent-distance of prop:A3-covariance. The revised identification of d_g as 'the flat geodesic distance of the metric determined by the jump covariance' is matched by sum_root_mul (sum_alpha alpha_i alpha_j = 8 delta_ij in the Lean coordinates, i.e. Q_h = (1/8) sum alpha (x) alpha = I, so g = Q_h^{-1} is the Euclidean inner product used by flatDistance). Scoped: the covariance identity and the convergence theorem are separate Lean statements linked through the common Space inner product; mesh index d = n + 1.

def:supp-current-polytope.title: Cycle-current polytope and its positive interior
def:supp-current-polytope.note: SimpleOrientation V E is a simple undirected graph presented by one orientation (tail, head) of each edge (no parallel edges, no antiparallel pair, hence no loops); incidenceReal is the real incidence matrix B : R^E -> R^V, B_{x e} = [tail e = x] - [head e = x], and incidence its complex copy. closedCurrentPolytope G c = {j | B j = 0 and |j_e| <= c_e for all e} is the closed polytope Jbar(G,c) (eq:supp-current-polytope-closed) and currentPolytope G c = {j | B j = 0 and |j_e| < c_e} is J(G,c) (eq:supp-current-polytope), with currentPolytope ⊆ closedCurrentPolytope. The revised characterization 'J(G,c) consists precisely of the currents with both directional fluxes c_e +- j_e strictly positive' is abs_lt_conductance_iff_flux_pos (|j_e| < c_e <-> 0 < forwardFlux = c_e + j_e and 0 < reverseFlux = c_e - j_e). currentPolytope_eq_fibre identifies J(G,c) with the complex-incidence GraphSpectralFibre via isStationaryCurrent_incidence_iff. Scoped: 'relative interior' is the definitional strict-inequality set (its topological identification with the relative interior of Jbar is not formalized); the arctanh-domain sentence is a remark.

thm:supp-graph-realization.title: Stationary Markov realization fibre of a metric graph triple
thm:supp-graph-realization.note: Revised to the closed fibre; every clause is covered. (R1) isRealization_reversibleRates: c/m is a stationary realization with detailed balance. (R2) isRealization_rates: every j in the CLOSED polytope Jbar(G,c) gives the stationary realization k = (c+j)/m with nonnegative rates (stationarity from sum_pairFlux_sub: sum_y (q_xy - q_yx) = 2 (B j)_x); 'currents in J(G,c) are exactly those with positive flux in both directions' is rates_pos_of_mem (=>) and IsRealization.currentOf_mem (<=), packaged as realizationEquiv. (R3) IsRealization.existsUnique_current: every stationary realization with masses m and symmetrized flux c (IsRealization: zero diagonal, nonnegative rates, mass stationarity, (q+q^T)/2 = c on edges and 0 off edges) is uniquely (c+j)/m with j in Jbar(G,c) (currentOf_mem_closed). (R4) dirac_rates: the Hodge-Dirac matrix of every current realization is dirac m c. eq:supp-realization-fibre RReal_graph = Jbar(G,c) is the explicit bijection closedRealizationEquiv : Jbar(G,c) ≃ {stationary realizations}, and J(G,c) ≃ {positive-edge realizations} is realizationEquiv. stationary_markov_realization_fibre bundles (R1), the open-polytope part of (R2), (R3), (R4) and realizationEquiv; the closed-polytope (R2) and closedRealizationEquiv are the separate cited lemmas. IsRealization.toStationaryRenewalGraph / isRealization_of_stationaryRenewalGraph tie realizations to def:supp-renewal-graph. Scoped: simple graph (the paper's 'up to unobserved parallel-channel refinements'), diagonal of k normalized to 0; 'strictly positive relative interior' is the strict-inequality set.

cor:supp-fibre-dimension.note: Revised statement proved for a connected simple graph G presented by an orientation (SimpleOrientation, as in def:supp-current-polytope), positive masses m and positive edge conductances c. fibre_affine_dimension_and_faithfulness bundles: (1) the closed polytope Jbar(G,c) and its relative interior J(G,c) both have affine dimension |E|+1-|V| = b_1(G), stated as finrank_R of the direction of their affine spans (closedCurrentPolytope_affineDim, currentPolytope_affineDim): both vector spans equal the REAL cycle space ker B (vectorSpan_*: every cycle current has a positive multiple in the open box around 0) and finrank_R ker B = |E|+1-|V| (realCycleSpace_finrank, rank-nullity for B and B^T with ker B^T = constants by connectedness); (2) (forall stationary realizations k of (m,G,c), k = reversibleRates m c) <-> |E|+1 = |V| (reversible_unique_iff_tree; tree = connected with |E| = |V|-1, transferred to realizations via existsUnique_current / rates_injective); (3) if |V| < |E|+1 (b_1 > 0) two distinct stationary realizations in J(G,c) share the Hodge-Dirac matrix (spectralization_not_faithful). Natural-number subtraction |E|+1-|V| is exact because |V| <= |E|+1 is proved for connected G (card_le_card_edges_add_one). Non-vacuity example: the one-vertex tree. Axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.

prop:supp-entropy.note: The revision restricts the statement to j in J(G,c), which is exactly the Lean hypothesis: sigma(j) = 2 sum_e j_e log((c_e+j_e)/(c_e-j_e)) (entropyProduction, entropyEdge) is nonnegative edgewise (entropyEdge_nonneg) and vanishes exactly at j = 0 (entropyProduction_eq_zero_iff) under 0 < c_e and |j_e| < c_e (the Lean does not even need B j = 0). Scoped: the formula is taken as the definition (its derivation from (1/2) sum (q_xy - q_yx) log(q_xy/q_yx) is not compiled); the added boundary sentence (extended value +infinity on Jbar(G,c) minus J(G,c) when a directional flux vanishes) is an interpretive convention that is not encoded - the real-valued Lean formula is only meaningful on the open polytope.

lem:supp-zero-affinity.note: Proved in the paper's generality: for a real oriented incidence matrix B : Matrix V E ℝ (finite V, E) and conductances c, a current j in the fibre (B j = 0 and |j_e| < c_e) whose affinity a_e = Real.artanh (j_e / c_e) is exact (a = Bᵀ φ for some vertex potential φ, i.e. [a] = 0 in ℝ^E / Ran Bᵀ) is zero. Proof pairs φ against B j to get Σ_e a_e j_e = 0, each term nonnegative and vanishing only at j_e = 0 (Real.artanh_nonneg/nonpos/eq_zero_iff). Connectedness is not needed for this conclusion (a = Bᵀφ = 0 already forces j = 0 edgewise).

thm:supp-nonlinear-Hodge.title: Affinity coordinates for a fixed-traffic Markov fibre
thm:supp-nonlinear-Hodge.note: Partial: for a real incidence matrix with B^T 1 = 0 and ker B^T = constants (derived from graph connectedness) and c > 0: coercivity of F_alpha + (sum phi)^2, existence and uniqueness of the mean-zero minimiser phi_alpha, a_alpha = a0 + B^T phi_alpha, j_alpha = c tanh a_alpha in the fibre with B j_alpha = 0 and class alpha, uniqueness of the current with class alpha, and Set.BijOn of the affinity map J(G,c) -> R^E / Ran B^T (nonlinear_hodge, affinityClass_bijOn, existsUnique_current_of_connected); missing: (1) the diffeomorphism clause: smoothness of j -> [artanh(j/c)] on the open polytope and of its inverse alpha -> j_alpha (the inverse function theorem applied to the Euler map phi -> B(c tanh(a0 + B^T phi)) whose derivative B diag(c sech^2) B^T is invertible on mean-zero potentials); (2) strict convexity of F_alpha on mean-zero potentials (log cosh strictly convex, B^T injective on mean-zero potentials); uniqueness was instead derived from the Euler equation
thm:supp-nonlinear-Hodge.plan: Prove StrictConvexOn for F_alpha on the mean-zero subspace (compose Real.strictConvexOn log cosh with the injective linear map B^T restricted to sum phi = 0). For the diffeomorphism, show the affinity map is ContDiff (artanh composed with the quotient map), compute the derivative of the inverse via HasStrictFDerivAt of the Euler map G(alpha_rep, phi) and invertibility of B diag(c sech^2 a) B^T on the mean-zero subspace, then use the implicit function theorem (or HasStrictFDerivAt.to_localInverse on the bijection) to get ContDiff of alpha -> j_alpha; package as a Diffeomorph / PartialHomeomorph with ContDiff both ways between the open fibre (an open subset of Ker B) and the quotient H^1.

cor:supp-faithful-modular.note: Re-verified against the new statement (editorial change): the enriched object is renamed S_aff(j) (graph triple plus affinity class) and the conclusion 'faithful on each finite graph fibre' is restated as 'the affinity class determines the directed generator throughout the strictly positive fibre' J(G,c) = {j in Ker B : |j_e| < c_e}, which is exactly the Lean CurrentFibre B c hypothesis of both cited theorems. Proved directly, bypassing thm:supp-nonlinear-Hodge: two currents in the fibre 𝒥(G,c) whose affinities differ by an exact cochain (same class [a] in H^1 = ℝ^E / Ran Bᵀ) coincide (strict monotonicity of artanh via Real.artanh_le_artanh_iff / artanh_injOn); hence for fixed (G,m,c) the class [a] determines the directed fluxes q = c ± j (forwardFlux/reverseFlux) and the stationary rates k_xy = q_xy/m_x (forwardRate/reverseRate of FiniteGraphSpectralUniversalityFibre, eq. supp-current-realization). The metric packet (C(V),H_{m,c},D_{m,c},J,γ) depends on (G,m,c) only, so this is the faithfulness claim. thm:supp-current-chain.title: Graph quotients and entropy contraction

lem:supp-general-core.title: Smooth-core consistency and the Wilson term
lem:supp-general-core.note: Partial: in the chart surrogate on the whole lattice Z^d with point sampling, for 0 < h <= 1, three bounds are proved. norm_covSymmetricDifference_sample_sub_le: pointwise O(h) consistency of the covariant symmetric differences. norm_covWilsonTerm_sample_le: pointwise O(h) Wilson smallness, eq:Wilson-core-smallness in sup form. norm_covariantWilson_sample_sub_densitySymmetricDirac_le: pointwise O(h) consistency of the covariant doubled Wilson operator with -(i/2) sum (c^j nabla_j + nabla_j c^j), with explicit constant coreConstant. These assume the LinkExpansion and ConnectionBounds hypotheses and C^3 sup bounds of psi and of c^j psi. Missing: (a) the L^2 estimate with the Sobolev norms ||psi||_{H^3} and ||psi||_{H^2}; (b) cell-average sampling S_h = (J_h^0)^* and the reconstruction J_h^0, which the paper uses precisely to avoid point evaluation of Sobolev functions; (c) derivation of the link expansion from exact inverse spin parallel transport; (d) Leibniz bounds for c^j psi; (e) the identification with U_rho D-hat_g U_rho^{-1}, which needs lem:supp-density-symmetric (conditional).
lem:supp-general-core.plan: Restrict to smooth compactly supported or periodic psi on a periodic box. Prove the cell-average versions of the centered-difference and second-difference Taylor bounds with integral remainders, controlled by local L^2 norms of D^3 psi, and sum over cells to get the h^d-weighted l^2 bound by ||psi||_{H^3}. This needs a Sobolev H^k norm on the box, e.g. via iterated derivatives in L^2. Derive U_j = I + h Omega_j + O(h^2) from the ODE of parallel transport with bounded Omega. Add a Leibniz lemma for the C^k/H^k norms of c^j psi. Finally, compose with an instantiated lem:supp-density-symmetric.

def:stable-spin-atlas.title: Compatible stable spin discretization
def:stable-spin-atlas.note: Partial: CompatibleStableAtlas encodes, in an abstract surrogate, the doubled Dirac operator D-hat as SelfAdjointResolventData with a dense core of 'smooth spinors', the space H^1 as a Banach space V with a compact map into H, and finite-dimensional stages with self-adjoint D_h and isometries W_h. thm:supp-compact-spin-resolvent.title: Norm-resolvent convergence for compatible stable atlases
thm:supp-compact-spin-resolvent.note: Partial: in the abstract surrogate CompatibleStableAtlas of def:stable-spin-atlas, the following are proved. eq:supp-global-norm-resolvent: tendsto_norm_embeddedResolvent_sub for every non-real z, with a compact limit resolvent. The proof follows the paper: uniform resolvent bounds, strong convergence by the core argument, adjoint convergence, collective compactness from (A1)-(A2) and Rellich, then the norm upgrade. circleRieszProjection_embeddedResolvent_tendsto gives norm convergence of the Riesz projections of the compressed resolvents on circles in the resolvent set of (D-hat - z)^{-1}. cor:supp-compact-spin-image.title: Conditional stable compact-spin approximation
cor:supp-compact-spin-image.note: Partial: ConvergentMarkedSpinDiscretization.approximation proves three things in the abstract surrogate. (i) Norm-resolvent approximation of the doubled spin operator by the stage operators for every non-real z, from CompatibleStableAtlas. (ii) Exactness of every metric head: pure-state Connes distance = graph distance. (iii) Uniform convergence of the metric heads to the distance of a compact chain (HasChains) metric space. convergentStableCompactSpinApproximation_forall gives the essential-surjectivity clause as a family statement. con:supp-Naimark-tail.title: Canonical minimal Stieltjes dilation
con:supp-Naimark-tail.note: Construction encoded, with its defining properties proved. Analysis/OperatorMeasureL2Completion.lean builds, for any positive-semidefinite-valued vector measure μ with finite variation (PosOperatorMeasure; PositiveTailMeasure.toPosOperatorMeasure), the pre-Hilbert space PreL2 μ of bounded measurable H-valued functions with the semi-inner product ⟨f,g⟩_μ = ∫⟨f, dμ g⟩ (form; on indicators it is the paper's ∑⟨ξ_j, μ(E_j ∩ F_k) η_k⟩, form_indicator_const; positivity for simple functions by SimpleFunc.induction and for bounded measurable functions by dominated convergence, re_form_self_nonneg), the Hilbert space K_μ = L2 μ := Completion (SeparationQuotient (PreL2 μ)) (quotient by the null space, completed) with dense embedding L2.mk, the bounded multipliers L2.mul g (‖g f‖_μ ≤ sup|g| ‖f‖_μ from positivity applied to √(sup|g|²−|g|²) f; multiplicative, unital, additive, adjoint = conj), the projection-valued measure P_μ(E) = L2.proj (multiplication by 1_E: self-adjoint idempotents, P(E∩F)=P(E)P(F), P(univ)=1, finitely additive, strongly σ-additive hasSum_proj), and V_μ ξ = [1 ξ] = L2.embed with B_μ = V_μ^* (compressB). The unbounded operator C_μ = ∫λ dP_μ is not defined as a LinearPMap (no spectral theorem in Mathlib); it is represented by its bounded functional calculus: resolventOp z = multiplication by (λ−z)^{-1} (the resolvent (C_μ−z)^{-1}, z ∉ [0,∞)) and heatOp t = multiplication by e^{-tλ} (e^{-tC_μ}); these multipliers are set to 0 on the μ-null set (−∞,0] so that they are bounded. Disclosed surrogate: the pre-Hilbert space uses bounded measurable functions instead of simple functions (the simple functions are dense in it, mk_mem_closure_sourceSpan), which yields the same completion.

thm:supp-Naimark-realization.title: Operator-measure realization and minimality

def:supp-rational-Hermitian.title: Normalized rational Hermitian dynamic function
def:supp-rational-Hermitian.note: Encoded: Q is represented by its Hermitian Laurent coefficients M_n at infinity (eq:supp-rational-Laurent; Q(z-bar)^* = Q(z) is coeff_symmetric, Q(infinity)=0 is strict properness of the expansion) with rationality encoded, per Kronecker, as finite Hankel rank (finiteRank); laurentDynamicFunction is the series -sum M_n z^{-n-1}. Hankel columns c_j(h), their span K_Q, the sesquilinear Hankel form with [c_i(u), c_j(v)] = <u, M_{i+j} v> (hankelForm_single_single), its null space, the quotient state space with the descended form (hankelStateForm), A_Q c_j = c_{j+1} (hankelShift, well-defined by hankelFormalShift_null_le) and Gamma_Q h = c_0(h) (hankelSource). Proved in addition: the null space equals the kernel of the formal-to-literal column map for Hermitian coefficients (hankelNull_eq_ker), so the quotient is canonically the literal column span (hankelStateEquivColumnSpace), and [A^i Gamma u, A^j Gamma v] = <u, M_{i+j} v>. Not encoded: the equivalence rational-function <-> finite Hankel rank (Kronecker) and the identification of the tsum with the rational function.

thm:supp-complete-rational-Krein.title: Complete normalized rational generalized-Nevanlinna realization
thm:supp-complete-rational-Krein.note: Proved for Q encoded as in def:supp-rational-Hermitian (Hermitian Laurent coefficients M_n at infinity with finite Hankel rank; H finite dimensional). A finite Pontryagin realization (PontryaginRealization) is a finite-dimensional Hilbert majorant N with an invertible self-adjoint Gram operator J (form [x,y] = <x,Jy>; a fundamental symmetry J^2 = 1 is the special case of a suitably normalised majorant, and the negative index does not depend on the majorant), a J-self-adjoint state operator A and a source Gamma; output Gamma^+ = Gamma^* J, Markov parameters M_n = Gamma^* J A^n Gamma (Hermitian: markov_adjoint), transfer function Q(z) = Gamma^* J (A-z)^{-1} Gamma. The canonical construction (Hankel state space on its Euclidean carrier, Hankel form as Gram operator, shift A_Q, source Gamma_Q) is NormalizedRationalHermitianData.canonical with: canonical_markov (L_Q A_Q^n Gamma_Q = M_n); canonical_transfer_eq_toFun = eq:supp-rational-realization, Q(z) = Gamma_Q^+ (A_Q - z)^{-1} Gamma_Q, proved as an identity of functions on the region ||A_Q|| < |z| where the Laurent series defining Q converges (both sides are rational, so this is the paper's rational continuation; the resolvent Neumann series is the reusable Analysis/ResolventNeumannSeries.lean); finrank_carrier and mcMillanDegree_eq_finrank_columnSpace = eq:supp-rational-degree (dimension = stabilized Hankel rank = dim of the Hankel column span), with mcMillanDegree_le_realization (every linear realization L A^n Gamma = M_n has at least that dimension) and canonical_isCyclic (source minimality); canonical_form_eq / negIndex_canonical_form (the Pontryagin form is the Hankel form and the negative index is its inertia, negIndex = largest dimension of a negative definite subspace); negSquares_toFun_eq_negIndex: the Nevanlinna kernel N_Q(z,w) = (Q(z)-Q(w)^*)/(z - conj w) (eq:supp-Nevanlinna-kernel) has exactly negIndex negative squares (sup of the negative inertia of finite kernel Grams) on every upper half-plane neighbourhood of infinity {Im z > 0, |z| > rho}, rho >= ||A_Q||, and negSquares_canonical_transfer_eq on the whole upper half-plane part of the resolvent set of the realization; mechanism: inner_nevanlinnaKernel (kernel Gram = Pontryagin Gram of the resolvent-source vectors), negIndex_pullback_le (a compression cannot increase the index) and resolventSourceSpan_eq_top (resolvent-source span = power-cyclic span, via the limit -w(A-w)^{-1} -> 1). Uniqueness: PontryaginRealization.existsUnique_sourceFixing_unitary: any two source-cyclic finite Pontryagin realizations with the same Laurent coefficients are related by a unique linear isomorphism fixing the source, intertwining the state operators and preserving the indefinite forms (the source-fixing Pontryagin unitary). Scoped: 'minimal' is read as source-cyclic (the paper's source minimality; observability is automatic from nondegeneracy, futureRead_separating).

thm:supp-pole-Hankel.title: Pole--Hankel invariants
thm:supp-pole-Hankel.note: PROVED as NormalizedRationalHermitianData.poleHankelInvariants for the canonical minimal realization P = Q.canonical of a normalized rational Hermitian Q (its transfer function Gamma^+ (A - z)^{-1} Gamma is the rational continuation of Q, eq:supp-rational-realization). New infrastructure: Algebra/RootSubspaceProjection.lean (Riesz projection rootProj f mu onto the root subspace R_mu = maxGenEigenspace along the sum of the other root subspaces, for any endomorphism of a finite-dimensional space over an algebraically closed field: commutes with f, idempotent, (f - mu)^dim kills its range, and the regular pencil (f - mu)(1 - pi) + pi is invertible). Predictive/PoleHankelLocalRealization.lean: principal-part coefficients C_k = Gamma^* J (A - lam)^k pi_lam Gamma and the PRINCIPAL-PART DECOMPOSITION transfer_eq_principalPart_add_regularPart: for every z != lam in the resolvent set, Q(z) = -sum_{k < dim N} (z - lam)^{-k-1} C_k + R_lam(z), where R_lam(z) = Gamma^* J ((A - z)(1 - pi) + pi)^{-1} (1 - pi) Gamma is continuous at z = lam (continuousAt_regularPart), so the C_k are the principal part of Q at lam (for a non-pole lam they vanish). (P1) finrank_range_localHankelMap: local controllability (range_localCtrlMap) and observability (ker_localObsMap) of the local realization ((A - lam)|R_lam, pi_lam Gamma, Gamma^* J|R_lam) follow from source cyclicity and nondegeneracy, so rank [C_{i+j+s}]_{i,j < dim N} = rank ((A - lam)|R_lam)^s for every shift s; s = 0 gives the local McMillan degree dim R_lam; by NilpotentHankel.card_chains_ge_eq_finrank_sub the differences of these ranks are the numbers of Jordan chains of each length. (P2) at a real lam the Gram of the local Krylov family is the principal-part Hankel Gram [<e_k, C_{i+j} e_l>] (gram_localKrylov_of_real), so neg(R_lam) = negInertia, pos(R_lam) = posInertia (subNegIndex/subPosIndex_rootSpace_eq_..._localHankelGram) and neg + pos = dim R_lam (nondegeneracy). (P3), (P4) as before (subNegIndex_poleBlock_of_pos, negSquares_eq_sum_localIndex). Scoped/disclosed: 'pole' is rendered as an arbitrary point lam (the statements are trivial when R_lam = 0); the uniqueness of a principal-part decomposition (that C_k is determined by Q alone, a textbook Laurent fact) is not separately formalised; the Jordan block sizes are rendered as the rank sequence of the nilpotent local state operator, and the count lemma takes the existence of a Jordan chain basis as a hypothesis (not in Mathlib); the Hankel operators use blocks of size dim N (any size >= the nilpotency index works).

cor:supp-all-rational.title: All finite rational Hermitian dynamics
cor:supp-all-rational.note: PROVED (sorry-free, standard axioms only). New file Predictive/DescriptorWeierstrassForm.lean (1511 lines) closes the general (non-primary) side and assembles the corollary; bundled statement RenewalGeometry.cor_supp_all_rational. Setting: H, N finite-dimensional complex Hilbert spaces (the paper's finite setting); a regular Pontryagin descriptor realization is DescriptorRealization (E, A, Gamma, J) with regular pencil; a finite rational Hermitian dynamic function is FiniteRationalHermitianData Q = P + Q_0 (eq:supp-rational-split). (1) WEIERSTRASS REDUCTION: for any regular D and any real regular point t_0 (exists_real_regular), with T = E (A - t_0 E)^{-1}, pi_0 the Riesz projection onto the root subspace R_0 of T at 0 and W its root complement, the Weierstrass multiplier M = (1 + t_0 T) pi_0 + T (1 - pi_0) is an invertible J-self-adjoint operator commuting with T and pi_0 (weierstrassMul, isUnit_weierstrassMul, J_mul_weierstrassMul; pi_0 is J-self-adjoint, J_mul_rootProjL); the infinity block is the compression of (T M^{-1}, pi_0 Gamma, J M^{-1}) to R_0 (nilpotent, weierstrassInf_A_pow_finrank) and the finite block the compression of ((1 + t_0 T) M^{-1}, (1 - pi_0) Gamma, J M^{-1}) to W (PontryaginRealization.compress: compression of a Gram operator to a subspace on which its form is nondegenerate, compressGram_isUnit); D.weierstrassForm is the resulting PrimaryDescriptor and isSourceFixingUnitary_weierstrass verifies IsSourceFixingUnitary (D.rightMul (K M^{-1})) (D.weierstrassForm).toDescriptor S with S x = (pi_0 x, x - pi_0 x) (primaryEquiv), exactly as planned. weierstrassForm_transfer: the primary form has the same transfer function as D at every regular point (a source-fixing unitary preserves the transfer function, IsSourceFixingUnitary.transfer_eq). (2) MINIMALITY of general descriptor realizations: DescriptorRealization.IsMinimal := the resolvent-source vectors (A - zE)^{-1} Gamma h over the regular points z span the state space (the paper's source minimality of thm:supp-complete-rational-Krein). It is invariant under right multiplication (isMinimal_rightMul_iff) and source-fixing unitaries (IsSourceFixingUnitary.isMinimal, .symm), and on a primary form it is exactly PrimaryDescriptor.IsMinimal, i.e. both blocks source-cyclic (toDescriptor_isMinimal_iff; the Laurent/Vandermonde step is inlL_A_pow_Gamma_mem_resolventSourceSpan via coeff_eq_zero_of_tendsto_zero for the polynomial part and the real-ray resolvent limit Gamma_mem_resolventSourceSpan_real / resolventSourceSpan_realRay_eq_top for the strictly proper part). Hence D.IsMinimal <-> (D.weierstrassForm t_0).IsMinimal (isMinimal_iff_weierstrassForm_isMinimal). (3) THE EQUIVALENCE eq:supp-all-rational-equivalence: existence: Q.descriptor (primary direct sum of the infinity chain of P and the canonical realization of Q_0) is a minimal regular descriptor realization of Q (FiniteRationalHermitianData.descriptor_isMinimal, eventually_descriptor_transfer_eq_toFun); every minimal regular D realizes the finite rational Hermitian datum D.toData (eventually_toData_toFun_eq_transfer), whose coefficients are determined by the transfer function (toData_coeff_eq_of_transfer_eventuallyEq); uniqueness: a minimal D realizing Q is equivalent to Q.descriptor by reduction to Weierstrass primary form followed by a UNIQUE source-fixing descriptor Pontryagin unitary (existsUnique_sourceFixing_unitary_weierstrassForm_descriptor), and any two minimal realizations with the same dynamic function have Weierstrass forms related by a unique source-fixing unitary (existsUnique_sourceFixing_unitary_weierstrassForm). Dimension: every regular realization of Q has dim N >= McM(P) + McM(Q_0) (mcMillanDegree_add_le_finrank) and every minimal one has dim N = McM(P) + McM(Q_0) (finrank_eq_of_isMinimal): the minimal realizations attain the minimum state dimension. DISCLOSED RENDERINGS: (a) 'same dynamic function' is rendered as equality of transfer functions for all large real t (a neighbourhood of infinity on the real axis; rational functions agreeing there agree everywhere); (b) the paper's 'unique descriptor equivalence' between non-primary realizations is read as reduction to Weierstrass primary form (the right multiplication (E, A, Gamma, J) -> (EV, AV, Gamma, JV) by the J-self-adjoint unit V = (A - t_0 E)^{-1} M^{-1}, which preserves the transfer function, followed by the source-fixing unitary x -> (pi_0 x, x - pi_0 x)) followed by the unique source-fixing unitary between the primary forms; the primary form and D.toData depend on the chosen real regular point t_0, but the Laurent coefficients do not; (c) the negative-index part of 'attains both minimum ... indices' is not formalised here (the index statements are the separately ledgered thm:supp-complete-rational-Krein / thm:supp-pole-Hankel results); (d) minimality is source minimality (resolvent-source span = whole space), as in the paper's proof of thm:supp-complete-rational-Krein.

prop:extension-indefinite-compression.title: Negative-square index under effective-space compression
prop:extension-indefinite-compression.note: Proved (extension_indefinite_compression) for a normalized rational Hermitian Q on a finite-dimensional H (NormalizedRationalHermitianData) and any bounded V : H' -> H with H' finite-dimensional (the paper's isometry hypothesis is not needed; finite-dimensionality of H' is implicit in the paper's finite effective spaces). (1) Q_V is again normalized rational Hermitian: NormalizedRationalHermitianData.compress has coefficients V* M_n V (Hermitian; finite Hankel rank via finiteDimensional_hankelState_of_realization from the realization on the canonical state space of Q with source Gamma V and output V* Gamma^+, exactly the paper's proof), and compress_toFun_eq: Q_V(z) = V* Q(z) V on the Laurent region ||z|| > ||A_Q||. (2) Index clause: negIndex [.,.]_{Q_V} <= negIndex [.,.]_Q (negIndex_compress_le; negIndex equals the number of negative squares of the Nevanlinna kernel on every upper half-plane neighbourhood of infinity, negSquares_toFun_eq_negIndex), and the direct kernel form negSquares(N_{V*QV}) <= negSquares(N_Q) on upperNeighbourhood rho, rho >= ||A_Q|| (kernel Gram congruence, negSquares_compress_le). (3) Degree clause: mcMillanDegree Q_V <= mcMillanDegree Q (mcMillanDegree_compress_le), where mcMillanDegree is the minimal finite realization dimension (lower bound mcMillanDegree_le_realization, attained by the canonical realization). (4) Composition: (Q.compress V1).compress V2 = Q.compress (V1 o V2) and V2*(V1* Q V1)V2 = (V1V2)* Q (V1V2) as functions (compress_compress).

thm:supp-common-source.title: Joint Gram classification
thm:supp-common-source.note: Proved in finite dimensions with E_a = C^{n a} (index types in Type, as required by the reused repo lemma source_kernel_realization_minimal_unique) and X = Sigma a, n a. Corr_X = {K psd, K_aa = I} (CorrelationSpectrahedron); G_X = Pi_a U(n a) acting by block congruence K -> D(g)^H K D(g) (gaugeAct), which preserves Corr_X (block_gaugeAct, gaugeAct_mem_corr); Stab(K) is a Subgroup (stabilizer). A joint realization of K on a common space C^C is S : Matrix C X with S^H S = K (columns over block a = images of the marginal basis), its realization space Ran S. Proved: the Gram of a realization lies in Corr_X iff its marginal blocks are identities (isometric V_a); every K in Corr_X is realized (by sqrt K) with rank = rank K; every realization's Ran S has dimension exactly rank K and rank K <= dim of the common space (rank K is the minimum joint realization dimension, attained by restricting to Ran S); two realizations are equivalent up to a marginal frame change g and a source-fixing isometric identification of the realization spaces iff their Grams lie in the same G_X-orbit (frameUnitaryEquivalent_iff; the identification is unique, exists_unique_range_unitary, via the repo's joint_source_unique_range_unitary); for a realization S of K, a frame change g is implemented by such a unitary on Ran S iff g in Stab(K) (mem_stabilizer_iff_residual). Modelling disclosure: 'unitary on the common realization space' is formalised as a source-fixing linear equivalence between the ranges preserving the ambient inner product (the repo's convention), and 'minimal' as restriction to Ran S.

cth:supp-pairwise-not-global.title: Pairwise positivity need not give a joint realization
cth:supp-pairwise-not-global.note: The explicit 3×3 real matrix M = !![1,-3/4,-3/4; -3/4,1,-3/4; -3/4,-3/4,1]: M *ᵥ (1,1,1) = (-1/2)•(1,1,1), hence Module.End.HasEigenvalue (Matrix.toLin' M) (-1/2); M is not Matrix.PosSemidef (quadratic form -3/2 on (1,1,1)); and for every i ≠ j in Fin 3 the principal block M.submatrix ![i,j] ![i,j] is Matrix.PosDef (all blocks equal !![1,-3/4;-3/4,1], whose form is (x₀ - 3x₁/4)² + 7x₁²/16). So pairwise-admissible Gram blocks need not assemble into a positive joint Gram operator.

thm:supp-finite-exhaustion.title: Finite stratified fibre in the fully reduced coordinate model
thm:supp-finite-exhaustion.note: Proved in the reformulation the paper's proof establishes. A fully reduced finite realization of the completed target is rendered by its retained data (FullyReducedRealization): a joint Gram point K in Corr_X (thm:supp-common-source, JointGram.CorrelationSpectrahedron) together with points of the five retained fibres J_X x M_X x P_X x C_X^cal x R_X, which enter as sets with an action of the gauge group G_X = Prod_a U(E_a); the gauge group acts on Corr_X by the block congruence of thm:supp-common-source (instMulActionGaugeGroupCorr; gaugeAct is a right action, composed with inversion to a left action with the same orbits, mem_orbit_iff_gaugeAct, and the same stabilizers, which are the residual gauge groups Stab_{G_X}(K) of thm:supp-common-source, mem_stabilizer_iff_jointGram). Real_X^{sharp,min}(S) is defined as the set of fully reduced realizations modulo simultaneous gauge equivalence (RealizationSpace, the orbit space). The theorem finite_stratified_exhaustion is eq:supp-finite-fibre: an explicit bijection stratifiedExhaustion : Real_X^{sharp,min}(S) = Sigma_{[K] in Corr_X/G_X} (J_X x M_X x P_X x C_X^cal x R_X)/Stab_{G_X}(K) sending the class of a realization into the stratum of the gauge orbit of its joint Gram point (stratifiedExhaustion_fst), with the strata indexed by the block-congruence orbits and each stratum quotiented by its residual gauge group; the quotient is stratified, not a product, exactly as the paper says. The general mechanism is the new reusable infrastructure Algebra/EquivariantOrbitDecomposition.lean: for a G-equivariant map pi : X -> Y, X/G = Sigma_{omega in Y/G} pi^{-1}(y_omega)/Stab(y_omega) (EquivariantMap.orbitDecomposition, with the fibre carrying the stabilizer action and orbitRelQuotientCongr transporting orbit spaces along equivariant bijections). Disclosures: the five factor classifications that the paper composes (graph inverse theorem for J_X = thm:supp-graph-realization, positive/Pontryagin memory classification for M_X = thm:supp-Naimark-realization and thm:supp-complete-rational-Krein, marked bundle descent for R_X = thm:supp-marked-bundle, now conditional_interface only for its spanning-tree chord normal form, which is not used since R_X is by definition the marked monodromy representation space) are cited, not re-derived: the factors are G_X-sets here, and the full-reduction hypotheses (null quotients taken, minimal Gram blocks, the finite separating family with trivial common kernel) are what justifies taking the retained data as the realization set; they are not themselves formalised, so the left side is defined as the orbit space of the retained data rather than derived from a Grand-tensor realization notion. The descriptor (pencil) part of the memory factor (cor:supp-all-rational, now proved) does not affect this statement either.

def:supp-compact-fibre-system.title: Compact finite-stage inverse system
def:supp-compact-fibre-system.note: Encoded as CompactFiniteStageSystem H (CompactFiniteStageSystem.lean): increasing finite-rank orthogonal screens P_n (P_{n+1}P_n = P_n) with P_n -> I strongly; compact Hausdorff topological gauge groups G_n acting continuously on nonempty compact Hausdorff factor spaces Corr_n, Cur_n (closed current polytope), Mem_n, Mark_n, Cal_n, Mon_n; strata Stratum n = (Corr_n x ... x Mon_n)/G_n (diagonal action), proved compact Hausdorff and nonempty (a continuous compact-group action on a compact Hausdorff space is proper: properSMul_of_compactSpace, t2Space_orbitQuotient); the orbit-type decomposition F_n = Sigma_{[K] in Corr_n/G_n} (J x M x P x C x R)/Stab(K) as a bijection (orbitTypeDecomposition); continuous restriction maps with r_{n,n} = id and r_{l,n} = r_{m,n} r_{l,m}; stable images F_n^[m], F_n^infty (eq:supp-stable-fibre-images); compatible self-adjoint stage resolvent data R_n(z) on P_n H (adjoint symmetry, resolvent identity) converging strongly to the transported limiting family R(z) with resolvent identity, adjoint symmetry, injectivity and dense range; compatible finite-trace stage weights (additive, positively homogeneous, finite on positive operators, retained on P_n, increasing) with normal semifinite extension tau = sup_n tau_n, finite on every screen; retained completed data with compatible stage coordinates and finite separating families F_n with trivial common kernel after quotienting by the displayed coordinates. Non-vacuity witness CompactFiniteStage.trivialSystem (H = C). Rendering disclosed: the six factors are abstract compact Hausdorff G_n-spaces (the concrete closed current polytope, weak-* compact tight memory sets with trace-mass bounds, marking/calibration and monodromy carriers are instances of these parameters, not constructed here); finite-trace = finite rank; normality of the weights is rendered by the monotone-supremum extension (sigma-weak lower semicontinuity of an individual weight is not encoded); 'retained quasilocal directions' are rendered by the abstract type Retained with coordinates and functionals.

lem:supp-fibre-pruning.title: Canonical pruning of compact finite-stage fibres
lem:supp-fibre-pruning.note: Proved. General form InverseSystem.fibre_pruning (FiniteInverseSystemPruning.lean, N-system of nonempty compact Hausdorff fibres with continuous bonds) and its restriction-map form RestrictionSystem.fibre_pruning / CompactFiniteStageSystem.fibre_pruning (CompactFiniteStageSystem.lean; restriction maps r_{m,n} with r_{n,n} = id, r_{l,n} = r_{m,n} r_{l,m}, continuous): each paper stable image F_n^infty = Inter_{m >= n} r_{m,n}(F_m) (RestrictionSystem.stableImage, identified with the k-step images via r_eq_iterBond / stableImage_eq) is nonempty and compact; r_{n+1,n}(F_{n+1}^infty) = F_n^infty; F_n^infty is exactly the level-n projection of lim_m F_m (compatible families for all r_{m,n}; every stable point lies on a thread, exists_sections_apply_eq, via the Mittag-Leffler stable-lift property); maximality: F_n^infty is itself a subsystem in which every point extends one step (hence indefinitely) and every subsystem T with T_n subset r_{n+1,n}(T_{n+1}) lies in the stable images. Non-vacuity: example in FiniteInverseSystemPruning.lean (constant unit-interval system) and CompactFiniteStage.trivialSystem.

thm:supp-semifinite-exhaustion.title: Completed retained-coordinate inverse-fibre theorem
thm:supp-semifinite-exhaustion.note: Partial, in the CompactFiniteStageSystem encoding of def:supp-compact-fibre-system. Proved: the inverse limit of the stable images is nonempty and compact (compactSpace_stableSections, nonempty_stableSections), and the full inverse limit is identified with the limit of the stable images (sectionsEquivStable). Coordinates are injective given the separation field and FamiliesFactor (coordinates_injective). The strict-rate physical part is transported along the equivalence (physicalPartEquiv). The retained weights increase to their sup extension. Componentwise form: inverse limits commute with compact group quotients (EquivariantInverseSystem.limitQuotientEquiv, componentwiseCompletedEquiv). Missing: the surjectivity half of eq:supp-semifinite-fibre is the hypothesis Tight, i.e. every compatible thread of strata is realized by retained data. Nothing derives it from the paper's tightness, resolvent, weight and transport hypotheses, so the boxed isomorphism is assumed rather than proved. Also, 'retained completed inverse fibre' is an abstract type Retained, not a concrete completed object.
thm:supp-semifinite-exhaustion.plan: Give Retained a concrete meaning: tuples consisting of a closed self-adjoint operator (or its resolvent family), a normal semifinite weight and a compatible thread of factor data. Prove the realization step. (1) A strongly convergent compatible family of stage resolvents satisfying the resolvent identity, adjoint symmetry, injectivity and dense range is the resolvent of a unique self-adjoint operator. This is a pseudo-resolvent lemma; Mathlib has no unbounded self-adjoint operators, so it must go via SelfAdjointResolventData. (2) The weights increase to the sup weight. (3) A compatible thread of factor data gives the completed factor datum, using the weak-* compactness and tightness of the memory factor for the measure component. Then replace Tight by the paper's tightness hypothesis on the memory factor.
